questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Norway because I wanted to be closer to wild nature and I wanted to try living in a more calm study environment than Copenhagen. The University of Bergen had some really interesting courses for me to take, and the nature looked amazing, which is why I ended up choosing Bergen for my 1.st priority.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a wonderful experience living in Bergen. The courses were interesting, truly beautiful nature was in my back yard, and people are welcoming and helpful at the university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit tricky to get the hang of where to get information, but it was quite easy once I got to know the campus, and where to look for it. It was easy to find e-mails of the people you could write if you had questions, and finding the information center on campus was quite easy as well. The website for my courses and information about where to find classrooms were easily accessible as it was designed the same as the one used by the university of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got emails with information on where to go get my student ID and where to find my classes, and it was easy to find the student information center, if i needed more assistance or guidance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend searching for housing early on in the process, to make sure you have a good housing option.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quite easy, as you got an email with the information you needed

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to the information center, upon my arrival, and they registered me online

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were staff at the information center who helped, and you could also write or call the information center, if you needed more information

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I chose the classes online, and was lucky as I got all my 1.st priorities

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend reading the emails you receive thoroughly and ask at the student center if you need additional help

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took MA courses with BA-students who took the class at a BA-level, which meant there was an additional workload to the MA-programme, but this was specified, and it was easy to find information about.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I have not before tried taking MA-level classes with BA-students studying the same class at a BA-level, but it worked quite well, and it was clear what skillset you should have once the class was finished. I had more exams than I have had at UCPH at MA-level courses, and this was a bit overwhelming in the beginning, but I adjusted quickly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU and EEA Institutional Law and Policymaking
Comparative European Institutional Law
Human Rights and Welfare Policies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For law students who are interested in EU and EEA law and International law, the courses i took was very interesting. You learn about the different organs and actors and the strengthes and weaknesses of these. I would highly recommend Comparative European Institutional Law, this is a class where you reflect about the strengthes and weaknesses in national constitutions, and why it works/does not work in their specific countries, which I thought was very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I needed a good winter jacket, and good winter boots and more practical clothing during this exchange than i thought. You should have a good set of rain clothes, gloves and a beanie, and stiff like that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some groceries are more expensive than in Denmark, but it is more or less the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great opportunities for sport and clubs and societies. All very easy to seek out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sammen provides opportunities for fitness and sports of various kind, and the University also provides different types of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are quiznights every week around campus and I would recommend going to those, also to meet other students and local students. I would recommend signing up for a sporting activity of some kind, also to get to know other students and to get a little study break.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on hikes! There are many cabins you can rent, and beautiful day hikes to do in Bergen. I would recommend the app UT to check out hiking routes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Norwegians and Danes are quite alike, and a bit reserved, but if you talk to people at events usually they are very welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend signing up for local activities like quizzes, social events etc. These are easily found on posters at campus, or ESN instagram sites, and on facebook.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any cultural differences challenging as such

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I felt a very strong urge to go explore the nature. This was wonderful, the Norwegians go for day hikes and smaller hikes every week, and it was inspiring and I would recommend going on walks and hikes in the Fjell at least once a week.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend going to explore the nature! It is truly amazing
Join some sort of social community, there are many, and you will get to meet a lot if nice people
Take advantage of the opportunities to do the various kinds of sport, like climbing, ice skating, swimming and winter bathing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be afraid to ask for guidance and help. Teachers and university staff are very nice and helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to experience a different kind of being taught, and to work and study with people from different countries and hear their perspectives on the studies we were doing. I learned a lot about people, study-methods, laws of different countries and it was very rewarding for me. I also connected to nature in a whole new way, and that was really amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite scary to be in a new country and being without my support system back home, but I learned to ask for help, and to jump into this experience with an open mind.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
